name: TeamStarWolf - Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Chain (October 2026) Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the case study of the October 2026 Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527). No source names ATT&CK ids, so every binding is the study's own. Score 75: a CVE record or government advisory describes the behavior. Score 50: Volexity's report describes it. Score 25: a capability, an assessment or a close-but-inexact fit. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

legendItems.label: 75: described in a CVE record or government advisory
25: capability, assessment or inexact fit, labelled in the comment

techniques.comment: Authentication bypass and code execution against the internet-facing appliance from 3 Oct 2026, CVE-2026-104935 (CVE record 13 Oct; Volexity 13 Oct). Sources: [3] [12].
Root through the dsinvoked broker trusting DSCache configuration data, CVE-2026-111357 (CVE record 15 Oct 2026; Volexity 13 Oct). Sources: [4] [12].
Data returned in the exploit's own responses with no separate channel (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026); CISA's revised alert cites data exfiltration (30 Oct 2026). Sources: [10] [12].
Ivanti debug log tampered with (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Recent entries selectively removed from the Linux audit log (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Renamed packet-capture tool run on the appliance (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Stored LDAP credentials extracted; LDAP queries for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
LDAP and HTTP Basic credentials and NTLM hashes harvested from traffic (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
LDAP and HTTP Basic credentials and NTLM hashes harvested from traffic (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Password spraying against directory accounts (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Logs reviewed for valid usernames (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Commands and results carried in the exploit chain's own HTTPS requests and responses (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Assessment: a zero-day chain developed for the appliance, with medium-confidence LLM use in exploit development (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Assessment: medium-confidence use of large language models for exploit development and post-exploitation (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Close but inexact fit: library code patched only in memory during exploitation and then restored, which the Integrity Checker Tool could not see (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [10] [12].
Uploaded Perl script runs a Bash script, which runs the next stage (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
In-memory Python script, run by the Bash stage, carries the privilege escalation exploit (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Python stage delivered Base64-encoded and zlib-compressed, then decoded on the appliance (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
LDAP and Kerberos helper scripts deleted after use; the root-stage payload unlinks its own file (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Renamed packet-capture tool and its capture files kept in a hidden dot-directory (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Active Directory queried through a compromised service account and the results exported (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
DNS resolver configuration exfiltrated and the victim's internal domains resolved (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
Appliance configuration and authentication data collected for exfiltration (Volexity, 13 Oct 2026). Sources: [12].
